name: Sec rules

subjectOf.text: The Form PF filing obligation is triggered by a bright line asset threshold: every registered investment adviser with more than $150 million in assets under management attributable to private funds at the end of its most recently completed fiscal year must file.
subjectOf.abstract: All registered investment advisers holding more than $150 million in assets under management (AUM) attributable to private funds at the end of their most recently completed fiscal year, are required to file Form PF with the SEC.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: assets under management attributable to private funds

subjectOf.text: Title IV exempts private fund advisers with less than $150 million assets under management from registration, and requires the SEC to weigh investment strategy, size, and governance in determining the systemic risk of private funds.
subjectOf.abstract: Title IV of the Dodd-Frank Act exempts private fund advisers with less than $150 million AUM from registration (Dodd-Frank Act § 408) and requires the SEC to examine factors including the investment strategy, size, and governance of an investment adviser
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
